title: Cubical augmentation denominators and tensor representatives
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the coherent profinite site, $r\geq0$, $J$ a normalized comparison between generalized-section and discrete $\mathbf Z^r$ actions, $C$ a cubical model with the cell coproducts, boundary, translation and contraction of [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-augmentation-evaluation], $K$ a finite subset-coordinate Koszul model [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution], and $B$ an equivariant unital $R$-algebra [lem-sfb-lattice-flat-twisted-chain-pairing]. Work in ordinary signed cochain tensors and derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $L=J(C.L)$, $X=tK(B)$ and $Z=B[0]$. Assume $B$ commutative and $B\otimes_R-$ exact. For every normalized roof datum $F$ of [def-sfb-lattice-cubical-multiplication-data], the comparison satisfies $\delta;b=a$, both $a$ and $b$ are quasi-isomorphisms, and its tensor-representative predicate holds. Thus the three ordinary tensor words are K-flat representatives and the canonical localization tensor comparison is invertible on all their pairs. Neither multiplication of the evaluation maps, nor equality of localized evaluation roofs, nor low-rank coefficient identities is part of this assertion.

proof.text:
Write $X=tK_B\otimes_R tK_B$, $Z=X\otimes_R L$, $Y=(tK_B\otimes_R L)\otimes_R(tK_B\otimes_R L)$ and $\delta=\tau(1\otimes\Delta):Z\to Y$. The denominators are $a=1_X\otimes\varepsilon:Z\to X$ and $b=(1\otimes\varepsilon)\otimes(1\otimes\varepsilon):Y\to X$, using unit identifications. The counit identity in step 1 gives $b\delta=a$. The evaluation theorem gives that $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism. To check $b$, forget the action and write $e=s\varepsilon$ and $dh+hd=1-e$ as supplied there, with $|h|=-1$ and $\varepsilon s=1$. On $L\otimes L$ put
$$H(l\otimes l')=h(l)\otimes l'+(-1)^{|l|}e(l)\otimes h(l').$$
The tensor differential gives $dH+Hd=(1-e)\otimes1+e\otimes(1-e)=1-e\otimes e$. On $X\otimes L\otimes L$ use $\widetilde H(x\otimes w)=(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes H(w)$; the same identity becomes $d\widetilde H+\widetilde Hd=1-1_X\otimes(e\otimes e)$. Thus $1_X\otimes(\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)$ has homotopy inverse $1_X\otimes(s\otimes s)$ after forgetting. Let $\rho:X\otimes L\otimes L\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be the signed middle interchange used in $\delta$. Then $b\rho=1_X\otimes(\varepsilon\otimes\varepsilon)$: on surviving degree-zero cube components its interchange sign is $1$, and all other components are killed by augmentation. Hence $b$ has homotopy inverse $\rho(1_X\otimes s\otimes s)$ after forgetting. Homotopic maps induce equal cohomology maps because their difference on a cycle is a boundary. Forgetting the action is exact and detects exactness by the restriction-calculus theorem, so $b$ is an equivariant quasi-isomorphism; no equivariance of $h,s$ is asserted.

proof.text: They use ordinary representatives for derived tensors: the pairing theorem says $tK_B$ is K-flat; the evaluation theorem says $L$ is K-flat. Any tensor product of these is K-flat, since applying its tensor functor to an acyclic complex is a succession of the given acyclicity-preserving tensor functors. Hence $X,Z,Y$ are K-flat and their ordinary total tensors compute the specified derived tensors. This proves the roof equality with its actual denominators, without invoking a separate comparison of derived cup products.
